17:14 Local Time, 15:14 GMT, 20:44 IST: Right then, that is Stumps on day 4. A dominant day for South Africa, who have put themselves in a commanding position and are firmly on course to take a 1-0 lead in the Test series. The highlight of the day was the 117-run partnership between Rickelton and Rabada, which shifted the momentum firmly in South Africa’s favour and put them in the driver’s seat. Rabada chipped in with a valuable 72, while Rickelton continued his fine form with a solid century. Bavuma, despite carrying a calf injury, then came out to bat and showed great resilience to bring up a fighting fifty. Dane Paterson’s valuable cameo added further impetus to the Proteas’ innings, helping them stretch their lead beyond the 150-run mark.

In response, South Africa’s pace attack put the Bangladesh top order under pressure, striking twice early. Marco Jansen accounted for Tanzid Hasan Tamim, before Kagiso Rabada bowled Mominul Haque, leaving Bangladesh reeling at 12/2. Bangladesh managed to steady the innings with a gritty stand for the third wicket, but Simon Harmer broke the partnership by dismissing Najmul Hossain Shanto, who was caught at slip. Rabada and Harmer continued to pile on the pressure, combining to remove Mahfijul Islam and Towhid Hridoy in the final session. Bangladesh ended the day at 100/5, still trailing South Africa by 57 runs.

Kagiso Rabada has been the standout performer of the match, making valuable contributions with both bat and ball. As South Africa head into Day 5, all eyes will be on the pace spearhead to deliver once again and guide South Africa to a series-opening win. Can Bangladesh’s remaining five wickets put up a fight and produce something special, or will South Africa continue to dominate and cruise to victory? We'll find out tomorrow. Do join us for all the action..

Day 5 || 09:15 Local Time, 07:15 GMT, 12:45 IST: Litton Das and Towhid Hridoy smashed centuries to propel Bangladesh to a formidable first-innings total of 400. South Africa, however, responded with an even stronger batting display, led by a magnificent 157 from Ackerman and a century (102) from Rickelton. Rickelton’s crucial partnership with Rabada further strengthened their position, helping South Africa secure a substantial first-innings lead.

Kagiso Rabada, who claimed a five-wicket haul in the first innings, continued to trouble Bangladesh on Day 4. The South African pace spearhead struck twice, dismissing Mominul and Hridoy to pile further pressure on the visitors. Simon Harmer complemented Rabada’s efforts perfectly, chipping in with two wickets of his own to keep Bangladesh under pressure.

Just as South Africa appeared to be firmly in control, deteriorating light conditions brought an abrupt halt to proceedings, with bad light forcing the players off the field during the final session of Day 4. At the time play was halted, Bangladesh were struggling at 100/5, still trailing South Africa by 57 runs. Given the rhythm and control Rabada and Harmer had found, the visitors could well have lost a few more wickets had play continued.

The worsening light conditions may have come as a timely respite for the visitors, offering Bangladesh some much-needed relief. South Africa are firmly placed to wrap up the remaining wickets without much trouble. However, all eyes will now be on the final day to see how the action unfolds and whether Bangladesh can stage a fightback..
